The expected palette must be kept in step with the design document by hand.

terms.meaning: a named value such as a colour or font size that the whole app reuses
a score for how far apart a text colour and its background are in brightness; higher is easier to read
a widely used accessibility standard that sets minimum contrast levels
a colour written as a hash sign followed by six letters or numbers

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loads the token stylesheet
sections.what: Reads the token stylesheet once so every later check uses the same text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond sharing one read across checks.
sections.watch_out: The file path is fixed, so moving the stylesheet breaks every check in this file.

sections.name: block, dark, darkMedia
sections.title: Turns theme blocks into lookups
sections.what: Builds lookup tables for the light theme, the explicit dark theme, and the dark theme used when the device prefers dark.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app can choose dark mode by user setting or by device setting, and both need checking.
sections.watch_out: The parsing is simple text matching, so unusual formatting in the stylesheet can confuse it.

sections.name: resolve
sections.title: Follows token references to values
sections.what: Follows a token that points to another token until it reaches a real colour value.
sections.why: Tokens can refer to other tokens, so the real colour must be found before checking contrast.
sections.watch_out: There is no loop guard, so two tokens that point at each other would make this function call itself forever.

sections.name: lum
sections.title: Measures colour brightness
sections.what: Calculates the relative brightness of a hex colour using the standard accessibility formula.
sections.why: Contrast ratios are calculated from brightness, and this is the standard method.
sections.watch_out: Only six-digit hex codes are handled, so a three-digit code or a named colour gives a wrong result.

sections.name: contrast, DESIGN_TOKENS
sections.title: Contrast calculation and expected palette
sections.what: Works out the contrast ratio between two colours and holds the expected palette from the design document.
sections.why: Keeping the expected palette in the test makes unexpected colour drift visible.
sections.watch_out: The expected palette is typed by hand and the test does not read the design document, so the two can drift apart.

sections.name: tokens: light and dark per DESIGN.md
sections.title: Light and dark token rules
sections.what: Groups the checks: palette match, dark theme overrides, contrast levels for text and personas, theme colour match, and the ban on pure black and red.
sections.why: Likely reason: together these rules protect the brand colours and readability in both themes.
sections.watch_out: The pure colour ban only scans css, tsx and ts files, so a colour in a json or html file is not checked.

summary: Checks the colour and type design tokens against the design document, makes sure the text colours meet readable contrast levels in both themes, and blocks pure black or pure red.
purpose: Protects the brand palette and the readability of text, so a careless colour change cannot slip into the app.
why: Likely reason: the design rules for colour and accessibility are easy to break by accident, and the checks catch it before release.
how: 1) Reads the token stylesheet and turns each theme block into a lookup table. 2) Resolves any token that points to another token. 3) Works out the contrast ratio for each text and background pair in light and dark themes. 4) Compares the colours with the expected list in the file. 5) Scans source files for pure black and pure red, and checks the Tailwind colour mappings.
inputs: src/ui/tokens.css, src/app/globals.css, src/providers/themeColor, and all css, tsx and ts files under src.
outputs: Pass or fail for palette matching, dark theme overrides, contrast levels, theme colour matching, and the pure colour ban.
risks: The expected palette is typed into the test by hand, so it must be updated when the design document changes. The colour parser only reads six-digit hex codes.
debug: If a contrast check fails, the failure message names the token pair and the ratio. Compare that pair in the token stylesheet and adjust the colour or the pair. If the palette check fails, compare the expected list with the design document.
